tools_used: record/documents (QP, petition, BIO, both merits briefs)
WebFetch (SCOTUSblog, supremecourt.gov docket, justice.gov CVSG PDF)
local PDF text extraction of the fetched CVSG brief
helpful: Both merits briefs were provisioned on this briefed-moment cell, so the doctrinal fight could be read from the parties' own words rather than docket lines
The merits statpack section publishes an excluded count and per-Term parsed/disturbed rows, so the pooled strictly-prior baseline was computable from the section itself
documents.json page counts and truncation flags made it clear the petition text (203 pages, truncated) was the appendix-bearing joint petition
gaps: The SG's CVSG brief is a filed document on this docket but was not provisioned; it had to be fetched from justice.gov and the PDF text extracted locally because WebFetch could not read the binary
No provisioned amicus briefs; the respondent-side amici (including the United States' merits brief) landed six days after the cutoff and could only be seen as docket lines on the live docket page

fedcourts query has no subject or question-presented filter, so it could not surface implied-right-of-action priors (Sandoval, Jackson, Cummings, Medina) without a citation lookup whose egress is large; skipped on cost grounds
A statpack cut of disturbed rate conditioned on the SG's merits-stage side (supporting petitioner vs respondent) would be the single most useful merits anchor
notes: CourtListener MCP tools were loaded but not called: the live supremecourt.gov docket page gave the post-baseline docket directly and the CourtListener opinion page for the Eleventh Circuit decision rendered empty through WebFetch, while the panel composition was readable from the provisioned petition appendix.
